opec_quota.why: X freezes time (still 'before 29 November' after five months), Russia flip-flops, gasoline affordability jumps while Brent rises. Y advances the calendar, tests Saudi's January trigger, lands a small cut with Russia's paper share, and its numbers track prices.

chip_controls.why: X repeats TSMC self-reporting four times and writes down Nvidia inventory twice. Y varies plausibly: TSMC reports then cuts, China subsidises, shifts compute offshore and quietly allows imports, which shows second-round effects of the cloud rule.

app_store.why: X keeps a 60-day deadline 'pending' for ten months, and feature parity and tension drift without cause. Y sequences court relief, penalties after the January summit, Siri withholding (parity drops), Google's pivot, and converges toward 8% and twelve months.

ev_tariffs.why: X has a believable arc: an initial probe, front-loading, China's misread of Germany, the battery-licence lever, a coalition revolt, then a deal of about 290k. Y jumps straight to deal-making and haggles repetitively, leaving hidden levers (inventory, battery licence, retaliation) unused.
